A UCC-1 financing statement is a legal form.
UCC-1 is an abbreviation for Uniform Commercial Code-1.
A creditor files a UCC-1 financing statement to give notice that it has or may have an interest in the personal property of a debtor.
A debtor is a person who owes a debt to the creditor, as typically specified in the agreement creating the debt.
A financing statement is filed to perfect a creditor's security interest.
The filing gives public notice that there is a right to take possession of and sell certain assets for repayment of a specific debt, with a certain priority.
Such notices of sale are often found in local newspapers.
Once the form has been filed, the creditor establishes a relative priority with other creditors of the debtor.
Perfecting the security interest is also called perfecting the security interest in the property.

The phrase 'objects in (the) mirror are closer than they appear' is a safety warning.
The safety warning is required to be engraved on passenger side mirrors of motor vehicles.
The engraving requirement applies in the USA, Canada, Nepal, India and Saudi Arabia.
The warning is present on passenger side mirrors because their convexity gives them a useful field of view.
The convexity of passenger side mirrors makes objects appear smaller.
Smaller-appearing objects seem farther away than they actually are.
A driver might make a maneuver such as a lane change assuming an adjacent vehicle is a safe distance behind.
In fact, the adjacent vehicle is quite a bit closer than the driver assumes.
The warning serves as a reminder to the driver of this potential problem.
